terms.comment: The everyday word of Cicero’s prose, with the indicative.
From fors sit an; in Cicero always with the subjunctive.

terms.register: vōx plērumque poētica: Verg., Hor.; also post-Augustan prose

terms.gloss: perhaps; the same word as fortasse, rarer

phrases.latin: forsan et haec ōlim meminisse juvābit
phrases.english: perhaps one day even this will be a pleasure to remember
Maybe it’ll rain; put your coat on.

short-e.html: Why fortasse, not fortassē: Lewis & Short prints a long final e but gives no evidence. De Vaan (2008: 236, s.v. fors) speaks of the word’s “short final vowel”, and verse proves it. In Catullus 85.1, Ōdī et amō. quārē id faciam fortasse requīris, the fifth foot -tasse re- must be a dactyl, so the e is short; Horace scans it the same way (S. 1.3.20, 1.6.98).
